title: Quenched disorder in polymerized membranes: from anomalous elasticity to a glassy phase
abstract: Polymerized membranes are paradigmatic fluctuating systems in which geometry, elasticity, and statistical fluctuations combine to produce anomalous long-distance behavior. In the disorder-free flat phase, bending rigidity increases at long wavelengths while in-plane elastic moduli soften. Quenched random metric and curvature introduce competing thermal and disorder-induced fluctuations. We review perturbative and nonperturbative field-theoretical approaches to these systems, from pure membranes to their disordered counterparts. Early one-loop studies identified a disorder-free fixed point, $P_4$, and a zero-temperature disorder-dominated fixed point, $P_5$. A subsequent nonperturbative renormalization-group analysis revealed a third fixed point, $P_c$, at finite temperature and disorder, governing a continuous wrinkling transition between the thermally dominated flat phase and a disorder-dominated glassy phase. Higher-order perturbative calculations also recover a $P_c$-like fixed point, with anomalous dimensions remarkably close to the reexpanded nonperturbative predictions. This scenario connects naturally with the wrinkling transition observed in partially polymerized lipid membranes. The three experimental scaling regimes of height fluctuations can be associated with $P_4$, $P_c$, and $P_5$, with theoretical exponents showing good quantitative agreement with measurements, particularly at criticality. Finally, we discuss the status of the glassy scenario, the unresolved discrepancy between perturbative and nonperturbative fixed-point stability predictions, and possible extensions to defective graphene and related two-dimensional crystalline materials.
summary: This work reviews the theoretical understanding of polymerized membranes under quenched disorder, predicting a continuous wrinkling transition between a smooth, thermally stable phase and a glassy, disorder-dominated phase. Using advanced Renormalization Group techniques, the authors map three distinct physical regimes onto three corresponding fixed points ($P_4, P_c, P_5$). The strong quantitative agreement between these theoretical exponents and experimental measurements makes this a key theoretical benchmark for disordered soft matter physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quenched random disorder modifies the anomalous elasticity of polymerized membranes, potentially driving the system into a glassy phase.
main_result: A continuous wrinkling transition is predicted between a thermally dominated flat phase and a disorder-dominated glassy phase, characterized by a novel fixed point ($P_c$).
method: The analysis employs advanced field-theoretical techniques, including perturbative and nonperturbative Renormalization Group (RG) methods.
model_or_system: The system is a polymerized membrane (e.g., lipid membranes, graphene) whose elasticity is governed by bending rigidity and in-plane moduli, coupled to random metric and curvature disorder.
key_observables: Height fluctuation power spectrum exponent ($\gamma$), anomalous elastic moduli ($\kappa_{	ext{eff}}(q)$), and the existence of multiple RG fixed points ($P_4, P_c, P_5$).
important_parameters: Temperature, polymerization degree, and the strength of quenched disorder.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the physical system onto a field theory framework and using RG techniques to identify stable fixed points.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the theoretical framework, first establishing the disorder-free flat phase physics ($P_4$), then incorporating disorder to find the critical point ($P_c$), and finally characterizing the low-temperature, disorder-dominated glassy phase ($P_5$).
why_interesting: The study of phase transitions driven by quenched disorder, especially the identification of a continuous transition point ($P_c$) separating thermal and glassy regimes, is highly relevant to understanding disordered quantum many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic RG topology of the quenched metric–curvature disorder problem. The dashed curve represents the critical separatrix, i.e. the stable manifold of the finite-temperature fixed point Pc; the arrows drawn along it indicate that RG trajectories on the separatrix flow toward Pc. The solid trajectories leaving Pc represent the flow along its relevant direction, toward either the thermal fixed point P4 or the disorder-dominated fixed point P5. The two sides of the separatrix define the thermal and glassy basins of attraction, respectively. The temperature and disorder axes are schematic, and the drawing does not represent the actual multidimensional coupling space.
